checked_sources.source: Maxime Haddouche, Benjamin Guedj, Online PAC-Bayes Learning, NeurIPS 2022 / arXiv:2206.00024v2
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified a direct answer for the past-only-prior frontier in generic online PAC-Bayes. The paper defines an online predictive prior sequence P_i with P_i measurable with respect to F_{i-1}; Theorem 2.3 permits these past-dependent priors and arbitrary evolving posterior kernels under bounded loss and dependent data. Corollary 3.1 gives a practical update trading current loss against KL(Q||P_i), and the special case P_i=previous posterior yields a sequential Gibbs/previous-posterior-as-prior update.

checked_sources.source: Maxime Haddouche, Otmane Sakhi, Sequential Off-Policy Learning with Logarithmic Smoothing, arXiv:2506.10664v2, 12 May 2026
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified the crucial boundary: Theorem 3.2 is simultaneous over every update k and every posterior Q but explicitly assumes a data-independent reference prior P. Therefore the 2022 predictable-prior theorem cannot be silently imported into this off-policy theorem without a new derivation. The same theorem also directly yields deterministic-policy certification when Q is an atomic point mass that has positive prior mass.

checked_sources.source: Karampatziakis, Mineiro, Ramdas, Off-policy Confidence Sequences, arXiv:2102.09540
checked_sources.result: Primary abstract re-verifies nonparametric, nonasymptotic off-policy confidence sequences valid uniformly over time and arbitrary stopping for contextual bandit policy evaluation, including gated deployment. No direct multivariate/vector-valued off-policy theorem was found in this pass.

checked_sources.source: J. Jon Ryu, Gregory W. Wornell, Gambling-Based Confidence Sequences for Bounded Random Vectors, arXiv:2402.03683
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified a general time-uniform confidence-sequence construction for bounded multidimensional processes with E[Y_t|F_{t-1}]=mu. This supplies a possible reduction route for a frozen off-policy target's vector reward after importance weighting, but the paper is not itself an off-policy theorem and does not certify adaptive policy-family search.

checked_sources.source: Dziugaite, Hsu, Gharbieh, Arpino, Roy, On the Role of Data in PAC-Bayes Bounds, AISTATS 2021
checked_sources.result: Primary-verified that data-dependent priors can materially tighten PAC-Bayes bounds when the data used to construct the prior are excluded from the empirical-risk term; the paper reports cases where this changes a vacuous bound into a nonvacuous one. This is corroborating evidence for strict lineage separation, not a sequential off-policy result.

candidates_new.mechanism: Learn or reuse a PAC-Bayes reference prior only from information available strictly before the current observation/batch. Represent the prior sequence P_i as F_{i-1}-measurable and update the next posterior against P_i, optionally using the previous posterior as the next prior when absolute-continuity support is preserved.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: The theorem explicitly permits past-dependent prior kernels P_i and arbitrary evolving posterior kernels for bounded losses and dependent data. In the previous-posterior special case, each update minimizes current expected loss plus KL(Q||Q_i)/lambda and remains an online predictive sequence. The source does not provide a universal numeric gain over a fixed prior; the benefit is a formal reduction of the relevant KL distance when past evidence predicts the next useful posterior.
candidates_new.scope: Generic online PAC-Bayes with bounded loss; not directly an off-policy contextual-bandit theorem. The prior at time i must be measurable from F_{i-1}; same-current-batch prior learning is not free under this result.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: A prior that adapts to the current evidence being certified can invalidate the guarantee. Support can collapse because the online predictive sequence requires an absolute-continuity chain. Under abrupt regime changes, previous-posterior priors may cause inertia. Most importantly, the 2026 sequential off-policy theorem currently fixes a data-independent P, so combining the two requires a new off-policy derivation.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: For iterative configuration optimization, allow the next evaluation prior to be shaped by completed earlier rounds, while freezing it before the new evidence arrives. This can lower complexity cost without a dedicated holdout purely for prior construction, but off-policy reuse should remain on the fixed-prior theorem until a predictable-prior OPE proof is available.
candidates_new.confidence: high for generic online PAC-Bayes; medium-low for off-policy transfer until rederived

candidates_new.mechanism: Preassign positive atomic prior mass to each deployable deterministic configuration/policy. In the sequential off-policy PAC-Bayes bound choose the posterior Q as a point mass delta_theta on the selected configuration, making the posterior-induced policy exactly deterministic rather than a randomized mixture.
primary_sources: Haddouche & Sakhi 2026 v2, policy representation and Theorem 3.2
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: For an atomic prior P with P(theta)>0, KL(delta_theta||P)=log(1/P(theta)). Substituting Q=delta_theta into Theorem 3.2 gives a simultaneous-all-k deterministic-policy bound whose complexity penalty is [log(1/P(theta))+log(1/delta)]/[lambda (k+1)m]. With a uniform prior over M predeclared configurations this becomes log(M)/[lambda N] plus the confidence term.
candidates_new.scope: Direct for finite/countable atomic configuration families that are represented by the theorem's predictor-policy mapping and remain in prior support. This is a derivation from the theorem rather than a separately named derandomization theorem.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: A continuous prior gives infinite KL to an exact point mass. A newly invented configuration with zero prior mass is uncertified. Very large candidate dictionaries pay a log inverse prior-mass penalty. Adaptive expansion after seeing evidence needs preallocated countable mass or a new evaluation lineage/prior before using new evidence.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: Use an atomic codebook prior over concrete automation configurations, optionally weighted by description length or structural simplicity. This preserves deterministic deployment while retaining same-stream sequential PAC-Bayes certification and makes candidate-family growth pay an explicit code-length-like complexity cost.
candidates_new.confidence: high for the mathematical specialization; medium for practical config-codebook design

candidates_new.mechanism: For a frozen target policy and several bounded outcome coordinates, transform each logged interaction into a bounded vector-valued off-policy score and feed that vector process into a joint gambling-based confidence sequence rather than splitting alpha independently across coordinates.
candidates_new.quantitative_or_formal_evidence: Ryu & Wornell give time-uniform confidence sets for bounded vector processes with constant conditional mean. Standard importance weighting gives an unbiased target-policy reward vector when logging propensities/support are correct. The combination is therefore a plausible reduction for a fixed target under stationarity, but no dedicated off-policy multivariate theorem or matched sample-efficiency number versus scalar alpha splitting was found.
candidates_new.scope: Frozen target policy, stationary target mean, correctly known/predictable propensities, and bounded vector score after any required weighting. If clipping is used, its induced bias/changed estimand must be explicitly handled rather than ignored.
candidates_new.failure_conditions: Adaptive post-hoc target search is not covered by the generic vector theorem. Large importance weights may violate practical boundedness/tightness. Correlated outcomes can help joint geometry but no guaranteed sample saving was quantified here. Nonstationarity breaks the constant-mean premise unless the estimand is reformulated.
candidates_new.transfer_hypothesis: For a frozen candidate batch, jointly monitor utility, contamination, reliability and cost as a vector certificate. Keep adaptive candidate generation outside this layer; only after freezing a candidate should the vector gate reuse its logged evidence under a validated off-policy score construction.
candidates_new.confidence: medium for the reduction; low for claimed efficiency until directly benchmarked

evidence_updates.update: The deterministic-deployment frontier is partially resolved for atomic candidate families. The 2026 sequential off-policy theorem already certifies every Q simultaneously; with an atomic prior, choosing Q=delta_theta directly certifies deterministic d_theta with finite penalty log(1/P(theta)). Randomized mixture deployment is only necessary when the useful deterministic member lacks positive prior mass or a continuous parameterization makes the point mass infinite-KL.

Past-dependent priors are formally allowed by the older generic Online PAC-Bayes theorem, but the current sequential off-policy theorem still states a data-independent P. Therefore same-stream adaptive posterior search is verified, while same-stream off-policy certification with a learned predictable prior remains an open composition rather than an established corollary.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Because Online PAC-Bayes permits F_{i-1}-measurable priors, the 2026 sequential off-policy theorem automatically permits a previous-posterior prior.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not established. Theorem 3.2 of the sequential off-policy paper explicitly assumes a data-independent prior P even though it cites online PAC-Bayes tools.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: A predictable-prior off-policy extension needs its own supermartingale/change-of-measure derivation before deployment.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A deterministic config selected from a continuous PAC-Bayes posterior inherits the mixture certificate for free.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: False in general. A Dirac posterior against a continuous prior is typically singular/infinite-KL. The clean deterministic route found here relies on positive atomic prior mass.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Use an atomic/countable config prior, retain randomized mixture deployment, or add a separate deterministic re-evaluation certificate.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: A direct vector-valued off-policy confidence sequence under adaptive logging and adaptive policy-family search was found.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: Not found in this pass. Dedicated off-policy CS results are scalar/policy-difference oriented; the vector result found is generic for bounded constant-conditional-mean vector processes.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Treat vector off-policy inference as a fixed-target reduction candidate only until a direct theorem or full derivation is verified.

deferred_or_negative_evidence.lead: Learning a data-dependent prior from any part of the same evidence is harmless if the prior helps compress the posterior.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.evidence: False without conditions. The verified online result requires P_i to be measurable before the current datum; the AISTATS data-dependent-prior result excludes prior-training data from the empirical-risk term.
deferred_or_negative_evidence.reason: Freeze prior lineage before the evidence it will certify, or pay a separately justified data-dependent-prior correction.

frontier: Find or derive a sequential off-policy PAC-Bayes theorem with P_k measurable from F_{k-1}, preserving all-k/all-Q validity under predictable logging; quantify its complexity term versus the fixed-P theorem and identify support-collapse guards.

Turn the frozen-vector off-policy reduction into a complete theorem: define the exact bounded vector score, prove its conditional mean under predictable logging, handle clipping/bias explicitly, then benchmark joint vector confidence sets against scalar alpha splitting under correlated outcomes.

Develop an atomic/countable configuration prior for adaptive deterministic deployment: compare uniform finite dictionaries with description-length/code priors and specify how unsupported newly generated configs force a new prior/evaluation lineage.

Stress-test previous-posterior/predictable priors under abrupt drift and recurring regimes; search for change-point/restart mechanisms that regain adaptation without discarding valid old evidence unnecessarily.

Continue the heavy-tail branch: replace bounded/light-tail off-policy scores with robust e-process or truncation schemes while retaining deterministic atomic certification and explicit support coverage.

Formalize the layered architecture without crossing guarantees: prior-covered adaptive search -> support/coverage abstention -> deterministic atomic or mixture certificate -> frozen multi-coordinate gate -> anytime baseline-difference check -> pathwise hard shield.

actions_taken_instead_of_stopping: Resolved the past-only-prior question at the generic Online PAC-Bayes level and then checked the current off-policy theorem rather than assuming the results compose.
Derived and source-checked a deterministic atomic-posterior specialization of the sequential off-policy theorem, materially narrowing the mixture-versus-deterministic frontier.
Searched directly for multivariate off-policy confidence sequences; finding no dedicated theorem, downgraded the result to a fixed-target vector reduction and preserved the missing-proof frontier.
Maintained a nonempty frontier covering predictable-prior OPE, vector OPE, atomic code priors, drift, and heavy tails.

exact_next_action: First attempt a predictable-prior extension of the 2026 sequential off-policy theorem by combining its LS supermartingale with an F_{k-1}-measurable prior kernel, checking whether conditional Donsker-Varadhan/Ville steps preserve the all-k/all-Q statement. In parallel, formalize the fixed-target vector off-policy score and verify the conditional-mean/boundedness assumptions needed by Ryu-Wornell. If either proof fails, identify the exact obstruction and fall back to frozen candidate lineages with atomic priors and separate scalar off-policy gates.
